subject: SRV record mapping and client-certificate routing for private endpoints
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Jared Cole <jared.cole@acme-health.com>
Date: 2026-12-19T09:18:00Z
Subject: SRV record mapping and client-certificate routing for private endpoints

Team — attaching a first-draft proposal for how we want to support private deployments where customers prefer service discovery via SRV records (rather than explicit FQDNs) and will authenticate clients with mTLS client certs issued by their internal PKI. High-level goals: keep minimal exposure on our edge, ensure we can validate client certs (or accept a mapped client identity) at the point of ingress, and provide a clear mapping from SRV -> backend pool/FQDN so internal metrics and traces work.

Key asks in the doc:
- SRV-to-FQDN mapping rules (priority/weight handling)
- Where client certificate validation happens (sidecar TLS termination vs ingress proxy)
- Trust anchor rotation and how we store customer roots/CRLs/OCSP responders
- Fallback behavior when SRV entries point to non-RW-managed names (customer-owned target hosts)

My initial take (summary):
- Prefer terminating TLS at our ingress proxy for single-tenant VPC attachments to preserve observability and centralize cert validation, but allow a sidecar mTLS mode for fully on-prem air-gapped installs.
- Use SRV records only as routing hints. Resolve target hostnames and canonicalize to an internal FQDN namespace we control for metrics/logging.
- Store customer trust anchors in an encrypted secrets store (per-customer entry) and add a certificate-rotation window (30d) with automated test-signing and OCSP checks.

Attachments: 20261219-srv-mapping-draft.pdf (design sketch) and tls-sidecar-vs-proxy-comparison.xlsx (matrix).

Please review and flag any operational or security gaps. Jared — looping you in for visibility; if Acme has specific constraints around OCSP responder access or root distribution, please call them out.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-19T13:04:00Z
Subject: Re: SRV record mapping and client-certificate routing for private endpoints

Thanks Evelyn — good draft. A few concerns from the serving/runtime and on-prem side: 

1) SRV semantics and client expectations:
- SRV weight/priority can change frequently. If we canonicalize to an internal FQDN per SRV target we need a TTL/refresh strategy that won't thrash our routing tables. Recommend a caching policy: min TTL 60s, max 5m, with exponential backoff on NODATA.

2) Sidecar mTLS mode caveats:
- If we let the sidecar terminate client certs inside customer networks, we lose visibility for a lot of tracing headers and token usage. We need mandatory header propagation hooks from sidecar -> app. Also, sidecar mode requires a small shim that posts a signed attestation token to our control plane to prove identity mapping.

3) Ingress proxy validation of client certs:
- Validating customer roots at the ingress scale means we could be doing OCSP/CRL checks per connection — expensive. Suggest we support OCSP stapling from customer-provided responders when possible, and otherwise perform batch validation via a background worker that primes an allowlist.

4) Secrets and rotation:
- Storing trust anchors is okay but KMS access patterns must be accounted for. We should version each anchor and include a roll-forward period: new anchor accepted for 45 days with old anchor still valid for at least 7 days to allow for slow-propagating on-prem devices.

I'll update the draft with these operational constraints (and add a proposed test harness for OCSP responder simulation).

-Karthik
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Jared Cole <jared.cole@acme-health.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T10:26:00Z
Subject: Re: SRV record mapping and client-certificate routing for private endpoints

Adding a short operational playbook and recommended defaults below (I will fold these into the PDF):

Playbook recommendations:
- Default mode: Ingress-proxy TLS termination (multi-tenant hosted)
  - Validate client cert chain against per-customer trust anchors stored in vault (KMS-wrapped).
  - Require OCSP stapling provided by customer if real-time revocation is required; otherwise run background OCSP polling and maintain a short-lived allowlist cached at proxy layer.
  - Map SRV entries to internal pool IDs: resolve SRV -> target A/AAAA -> canonicalize to internal hostname (rw-svc-<acct>-<pool>.internal) and inject tags for metrics.

- Sidecar TLS termination (on-prem / air-gapped):
  - Sidecar validates client certs locally against customer's root and sends an attestation header (X-RW-Attest) signed by sidecar key. Control plane verifies attestation with short TTL tokens.
  - Sidecar mode requires a bootstrap API for trust anchor upload via customer admin or SFTP in fully air-gapped installs.

Operational controls:
- Rotation window: 45-day roll-forward, 7-day overlap for trust anchor rotation.
- Health checks: periodically validate sample client cert chains against stored anchors and run a synthetic connection test through SRV -> proxy -> backend.
- Escalation: if OCSP responder unreachable for >12 hours, circuit to sidecar-only or deny new connections depending on customer policy.

Action items:
- Karthik: add caching TTLs and OCSP batch validation design.
- Marissa: produce a short customer-facing page describing how to publish SRV records and expected TTL semantics; include an upload flow for trust anchors.
- Evelyn: confirm acceptable overlap windows and whether security wants shorter windows for HIPAA customers.

Jared — can you confirm Acme's internal PKI rotation cadence and whether you can provide an OCSP stapling endpoint for our proxy? If not, we can recommend the background-polling option in the onboarding doc.

-Jonas
From: Jared Cole <jared.cole@acme-health.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-21T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SRV record mapping and client-certificate routing for private endpoints

Thanks for the thorough plan — this matches what our security/compliance team wants to see. Quick answers: 
- Acme rotates root anchors annually and issues leaf certs quarterly. We can publish an OCSP responder for the environment Redwood will use; I expect NetOps to allow access from your proxy IPs.
- For SRV TTLs, our current tooling churns SRV entries on deploy but keeps TTLs at 60s; the caching approach Karthik suggested should be fine.
- We prefer ingress-proxy termination for hosted VPC attachments (observability is important for our audits). For fully air-gapped racks we'll take sidecar mode and can upload trust anchors over SFTP during setup.

I'll attach Acme's PKI onboarding checklist offline — sending it to Marissa and Evelyn directly.

-Jared
